children: ) OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei are taking the AI safety debate to the UN Security Council on Wednesday, as governments confront how increasingly powerful models could affect national and international security.

The executives are expected to brief the 15-member council alongside Hugging Face co-founder Clement Delangue and AI researcher Yoshua Bengio. Reuters reported that representatives from Chinese AI developers DeepSeek and Moonshot were also invited, putting competing U.S. and Chinese approaches to frontier AI in the same global forum.
Altman is expected to advocate for common benchmarks that governments and developers could use to measure increasingly advanced AI capabilities and evaluate whether adequate safeguards are in place.

That could become important for investors because standardized testing may eventually influence when cutting-edge models can be released, how extensively they must be evaluated beforehand, and how much developers spend on safety infrastructure.

The discussion comes amid growing concern that more autonomous AI systems could eventually act in ways developers struggle to control, potentially creating cybersecurity or national-security risks. Anthropic's Amodei has separately called for companies to slow the pace of capability development and give governments and researchers more time to manage potential risks.
Governments are far from aligned on how aggressively to respond.

President Donald Trump told the UN General Assembly Tuesday that his administration opposes new broad restrictions that could slow U.S. AI development, while saying authorities would monitor the industry and could intervene where necessary. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, by contrast, has called for stronger international governance and independent oversight of advanced AI risks.

title: OpenAI, Anthropic Take AI Risk Debate to UN
